checkup.title: Financial health check-up
checkup.intro: Your score across eight dimensions, built from the data you have entered. Every run is kept so you can see what changed.
checkup.noneBody: Run your first check-up to get a score, the risks that matter most and a prioritised plan.
checkup.noDataBody: You can run a check-up now, but the score will be low-confidence until you add your income, expenses and savings.
checkup.justRan: Your check-up is done. The plan has been updated with the new numbers.
checkup.noPrevious: This is your first run; the next one will show what changed.
checkup.assumesRetirement: This assumes you retire at {retireAt}, live to {lifeExpectancy}, prices rise {inflation}% a year and savings earn {postReturn}% after retirement, starting from today's expenses of ₹{expenses} a month.
checkup.noRisks: Every dimension is in good shape.
checkup.noStrengths: No dimension scores 70 or more yet; the plan shows where to start.
checkup.nothingChanged: No dimension moved between these two runs.

cashflow.good: You save a healthy share of income and essentials leave room to invest.
cashflow.watch: Savings are positive but below the 20% that funds every other goal.
cashflow.act: Expenses are eating most or all of income; this comes before anything else.
cashflow.unknown: Not scored yet: add your income and monthly expenses.

emergency.good: Your liquid savings cover the target months of essential expenses.
emergency.watch: There is a cushion, but a long illness or job gap would run it dry.
emergency.act: Little or no emergency fund; one bad month would mean borrowing.
emergency.unknown: Not scored yet: add your bank balances, deposits and expenses.

debt.good: EMIs are a manageable share of income and there is no high-cost debt.
debt.watch: Debt is serviceable but EMIs or costly loans are starting to crowd out saving.
debt.act: High-cost or revolving debt, or EMIs above 35% of income, need clearing first.
debt.unknown: Not scored yet: add your income so EMIs can be compared with it.

insurance.good: Life and health cover are close to what your family would need.
insurance.watch: Some cover is in place but short of the recommended amounts.
insurance.act: A large protection gap: one event could undo everything else.
insurance.unknown: Not scored yet: add your life and health insurance policies.

investments.good: Your mix is close to the age-based target and cash is put to work.
investments.watch: The mix has drifted or cash is sitting idle beyond the emergency fund.
investments.act: Allocation is far from target or most money is idle; a plan is needed.
investments.unknown: Not scored yet: add your bank savings and any investments.

retirement.good: On the current path you are on track for the retirement corpus you need.
retirement.watch: Between 70% and 100% of the needed corpus; a higher SIP closes the gap.
retirement.act: Well under 70% of the needed corpus on the current path.
retirement.unknown: Not scored yet: add EPF, PPF, NPS or other investments.

goals.good: Most of your goal value is funded on the current trajectory.
goals.watch: Some goals will fall short unless SIPs rise or dates move.
goals.act: Most goals are unfunded on the current path.
goals.unknown: No goals yet, so this is not scored. Add a goal to see whether it is on track.

hygiene.good: Nominations and basic estate paperwork are in place.
hygiene.watch: One of nominations or a will is missing.
hygiene.act: Nominations and a will are missing; both are cheap to fix.
hygiene.unknown: Not scored yet: record whether nominees are set on your accounts and policies.

plan.title: Recommended plan
plan.intro: One ordered checklist from your latest check-up, in the standard personal-finance sequence. Completed items stay done when you re-run.
plan.noPlanBody: Run a check-up and your plan appears here, ordered by what matters most.
plan.basedOn: Based on your latest score of {score}
plan.projected: If you complete the next {count} items your score could reach about {score}
plan.disclaimer: This plan is educational and generated by rules on your own numbers. It is not regulated financial advice; speak to a SEBI-registered adviser before large decisions.
plan.snoozeOver: Snooze period is over; this item is back on the list.

assumes.retirementSip: This assumes you retire at {retireAt}, live to {lifeExpectancy}, prices rise {inflation}% a year and savings earn {postReturn}% after retirement, starting from today's expenses of ₹{expenses} a month.
assumes.raiseTermCover: This is {multiple}× your yearly take-home income of ₹{annual}. The calculator also counts your loans, goals and savings.
assumes.raiseHealthCover: The recommended amount is ₹{target} for a family in a tier {tier} city, before any top-up for age.

titles.retirementSip: Start or raise the retirement SIP

fixOverspend.1: List the last three months of spending by category from bank and card statements.
fixOverspend.2: Cut or pause the largest discretionary items until income covers everything.
fixOverspend.3: Move the fixed expenses to a separate account funded on salary day.

clearHighCostDebt.1: List every loan with its rate; the highest rate goes first.
clearHighCostDebt.2: Pay the full card bill, not the minimum due, and stop new card spending.
clearHighCostDebt.3: Consider a balance transfer or a lower-rate loan to replace the costliest debt.

raiseTermCover.1: Work out the gap: 10 to 15 times annual income plus outstanding loans, minus existing cover.
raiseTermCover.2: Compare three insurers on claim-settlement ratio and premium for a plain term plan.
raiseTermCover.3: Declare health and habits honestly so the claim is never disputed.

raiseHealthCover.1: Check what the employer plan covers and whether it continues after leaving the job.
raiseHealthCover.2: Buy a family floater or individual policies that reach the recommended amount for your city.
raiseHealthCover.3: Add a super top-up once the base policy is in place.

setNominations.1: List every bank account, deposit, mutual fund, demat, EPF, PPF and policy.
setNominations.2: Add or update a nominee on each, online where possible.
setNominations.3: Keep one list of accounts and nominees where your family can find it.

buildEmergencyFund.1: Set the target: the months shown times monthly essential expenses.
buildEmergencyFund.2: Open a sweep-in FD or a liquid fund kept separate from spending money.
buildEmergencyFund.3: Automate a monthly transfer until the target is reached.

reduceEmiLoad.1: Prepay the loan with the highest rate using any lump sum or bonus.
reduceEmiLoad.2: Ask the lender about a longer tenure or a lower rate after a rate change.
reduceEmiLoad.3: Avoid new loans until EMIs are under 35% of take-home income.

raiseSavingsRate.1: Set up a SIP or transfer on salary day for the difference.
raiseSavingsRate.2: Raise it every time income rises, before lifestyle catches up.
raiseSavingsRate.3: Review subscriptions and recurring spends every quarter.

rebalance.1: Compare your equity share with the age-based target shown.
rebalance.2: Direct new SIPs to the under-weight asset class first.
rebalance.3: Shift existing money gradually, minding exit loads and capital-gains tax.

startInvesting.1: Keep the emergency fund in place first; invest only money you will not need for five years or more.
startInvesting.2: Start a monthly SIP in a low-cost equity index fund for the equity share.
startInvesting.3: Put the rest in PPF or a debt fund, and raise the SIP as income grows.

deployIdleCash.1: Keep the emergency fund aside; the rest is what can be invested.
deployIdleCash.2: Choose the goal or asset class the money belongs to.
deployIdleCash.3: Move it in over a few months through an STP or staggered lumpsums.

fundGoals.1: Open each goal to see the monthly amount it needs.
fundGoals.2: Raise SIPs on the Must goals first.
fundGoals.3: Push out the date or trim the amount of Nice-to-have goals that do not fit.

retirementSip.1: Use the retirement calculator to confirm the corpus and monthly amount.
retirementSip.2: Raise EPF voluntary contributions, NPS or an equity index fund SIP.
retirementSip.3: Increase the SIP by 10% a year as income grows.

writeWill.1: List assets, liabilities and who should receive what.
writeWill.2: Write a simple will; a template or a lawyer for an hour is enough for most families.
writeWill.3: Sign it before two witnesses and tell your family where it is.

fillGaps.1: Open My data and add what is missing: insurance policies, investments, EPF, PPF or NPS, and goals.
fillGaps.2: Rough figures are fine; you can correct them later.
fillGaps.3: Re-run the check-up to see the full score and plan.

annualReview.1: Update income, expenses, investments and policies once a year.
annualReview.2: Re-run the check-up and compare with the previous one.
annualReview.3: Re-run after any life event: marriage, a child, a new job or a home.

basis.defaults: standard planning rules, not your figures

rules.fix-overspend: Expenses including EMIs are higher than take-home income.
rules.clear-high-cost-debt: Some debt costs more than 15% a year or is a revolving card balance.
rules.raise-term-cover: Life cover is below 10 times yearly take-home income.
rules.raise-health-cover: Health cover is below the recommended amount for your city.
rules.set-nominations: At least one account, investment or policy has no nominee recorded.
rules.build-emergency-fund: Liquid savings cover fewer than 6 months of essential expenses.
rules.reduce-emi-load: EMIs take more than 35% of take-home income.
rules.raise-savings-rate: Savings rate is below 20% of take-home income.
rules.start-investing: Nothing is invested yet, so the mix is far from the age-based target.
rules.rebalance: Equity share is more than 10 points away from the age-based target.
rules.deploy-idle-cash: Cash beyond six months of essentials is more than 10% of financial assets.
rules.fund-goals: Less than 80% of goal value is funded on the current path.
rules.retirement-sip: The projected corpus is below the corpus needed.
rules.write-will: No will, and you are 40 or older or have dependants.
rules.fill-gaps: One or more dimensions could not be scored from the data entered.
rules.annual-review: Always included: a yearly review keeps every figure current.

benefit.fixOverspend: Stops the slide into debt; every rupee of surplus then funds the rest of the plan.
benefit.clearHighCostDebt: Saves the interest you pay at 15% or more, which no safe investment can beat.
benefit.raiseTermCover: Your family's income continues if you are not there; the premium is small at your age.
benefit.raiseHealthCover: One hospital stay stops being a reason to borrow or sell investments.
benefit.setNominations: Your family can claim what is theirs without a court process.
benefit.buildEmergencyFund: A job gap or illness no longer forces a loan or a sold investment.
benefit.reduceEmiLoad: Frees monthly cash flow and lowers the risk of a missed payment.
benefit.raiseSavingsRate: Each extra 1% saved compounds for decades; 20% is the usual minimum.
benefit.startInvesting: Money starts growing ahead of inflation instead of losing value in a savings account.
benefit.rebalance: Keeps risk in line with your age, so a market fall does not hit harder than it should.
benefit.deployIdleCash: Idle cash loses to inflation; put to work it could earn several percent more a year.
benefit.fundGoals: Goals arrive on time instead of being cut or pushed out at the last minute.
benefit.retirementSip: Closes the retirement gap while time is on your side; waiting raises the monthly amount.
benefit.writeWill: Your wishes decide what happens to your assets, and your family avoids disputes.
benefit.fillGaps: A fuller picture; unscored dimensions may hide the biggest risk.
benefit.annualReview: Catches changes in income, prices and family early, before they derail the plan.

goals.title: Goals
goals.intro: A goal is an amount on a date. The planner inflates today's cost, suggests a mix for the horizon and tells you the monthly amount needed.
goals.newIntro: Pick a template, enter today's cost and a date. Inflation and the asset mix are pre-filled from the rule pack and can be changed.
goals.noneBody: Add your first goal, from an emergency fund to a child's education or retirement, and the planner will tell you what it takes each month.

conflict.title: Your goals need more than you can invest each month
conflict.body: Together they need {required} a month; your current investable surplus is about {surplus}.
conflict.trim: Nice-to-have goals you could push out or trim: {names}.

goals.neverReaches: The current path never reaches the target; set a monthly amount.
goals.aheadBy: About {months} months ahead of the date
goals.archiveHint: Archived goals leave the dashboard and the check-up.

hints.member: Link the goal to a family member where it helps, such as a child's education.
hints.targetToday: What it would cost if you paid today; the planner inflates it to the date.
hints.inflationPct: Education and healthcare inflate faster than general prices.
hints.flexibilityYears: 0 for a fixed date; otherwise how many years it could move.
hints.assignedAmount: Existing savings or investments earmarked for this goal.
hints.monthlySip: Your current SIP or transfer for this goal, if any.

detail.projected: Projected value on the current path
detail.note: Returns are long-run assumptions from the rule pack, not promises. The mix de-risks as the date approaches, so the expected return steps down in the last years.

dashboard.addDataBody: Add your income, expenses and savings to get a confident score.
dashboard.runFirstBody: Your data is in; a check-up takes a moment and gives you a score and a plan.
dashboard.runFirstNoData: You can run it now for a rough score, or add your data first for a confident one.
dashboard.noRisks: No dimension needs attention right now.
dashboard.allDone: Every plan item is done or parked. Re-run the check-up to refresh it.
dashboard.scoreAfterStep: Finish step 1 and your score could go from {from} to about {to}.
dashboard.noGoals: No goals yet. A goal is an amount on a date; the planner does the rest.

formula.savingsRate: (take-home income − monthly expenses including EMIs) ÷ take-home income.
formula.essentialShare: Essential expenses ÷ take-home income. Essentials are the expenses you marked essential plus EMIs; without that split, 60% of all expenses.
formula.emergencyMonths: Liquid savings ÷ essential monthly expenses. Liquid savings are cash, deposits and low-risk debt funds with no lock-in.
formula.highCostDebtShare: Loans above 15% a year or revolving card balances ÷ all outstanding debt.
formula.lifeCoverMultiple: Life cover (term and endowment sums assured) ÷ yearly take-home income.
formula.healthCoverRatio: Health cover of the least-covered member ÷ the recommended cover for your city tier.
formula.allocationDrift: Difference between your equity share and the age-based target (100 − age, within the band below).
formula.equityShare: Equity investments ÷ all financial assets (cash, deposits and investments, excluding property).
formula.targetEquity: 100 − age, as a percentage, kept within the band below.
formula.idleCashShare: Liquid savings beyond six months of essentials ÷ all financial assets.
formula.retirementReadiness: Projected corpus at retirement ÷ corpus needed. The corpus needed funds today's expenses, inflated to retirement, through to life expectancy.
formula.projectedCorpus: Retirement savings plus equity and debt investments grown at the balanced return, plus the retirement SIP, until retirement age.
formula.corpusNeeded: Today's yearly expenses inflated to retirement, then the lump sum that pays that rising amount every year until life expectancy.
formula.goalReadiness: For each goal: what assigned savings and the SIP grow to by the target date ÷ the inflated cost; totalled across goals.
formula.nominationsSet: Yes when every account, investment and policy you recorded has a nominee.
formula.willInPlace: From your profile answer. Under 40 with no dependants counts as not yet expected.

input.retirementCorpus: EPF, PPF, NPS and retirement-tagged investments

assumption.termCoverMultiple: Target life cover, times yearly income
